# Security boundaries

Raw manifests are length-bounded data and are passed to versioned prompt templates only as structured variables. They cannot select a prompt, provider, tool, skill, runtime image, validator engine, or system instruction.

The v2 orchestration object is a strict PII-free intent containing only schema,
trigger, correlation UUID, exact surface, and optional desired difficulty.
Unknown nested fields are rejected, so student IDs, profiles, mastery/path
snapshots, conversations, and additional URLs cannot enter that channel. The
model may see this bounded object but cannot override its surface; the server
reapplies trusted intent before validation and staging.

All sibling HTTP calls require an explicit internal token, use timeouts, and cap response bodies. Practice staging uses the dedicated LW_PRACTICE_TZ_TOKEN credential, separate from the broad TZ inbound token; Practice accepts it only on the staging mutation. Runtime profiles and validation engines are selected only from authenticated capability catalogs. Selected learning targets must be members of the bounded discovery response and are exact-resolved again. Contract/capability digests and verification receipts are format-checked, content-addressed, and bound to the exact submitted case set. Fixture workspaces are isolated, TTL-bound, path-validated, and deleted best-effort after verification; TTL cleanup covers process crashes.

Public authoring responses exclude reference solutions, negative fixtures, hidden checks, provider raw output, and internal failure detail. The dedicated `student-technical-task-view.v1` type contains only `student_instruction`; it has no serializable internal step, hint, action, concept, verification, or private-evaluation fields. A separate full TechnicalTask route exists for trusted internal consumers. Before READY, the domain gate also rejects meaningful verbatim reference-file content found in the public instruction.
